comparisons.success_condition: PR-601 scores dimensional accuracy, angular alignment, gentle contact, and release/rest placement; it does not test a locked adjustable stop.
comparisons.reason: Force-controlled measurement is a different tested ability from mechanically locking and functionally verifying an adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Compress and fit a spring tension rod level between cupboard walls, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-716 requires bimanual compression, spatial alignment, and controlled release under spring force; the candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench manipulation and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-716 requires both caps pressing the walls at the marked height while the rod supports itself; the candidate requires nut retention, target angle, and repeatable cycles.

comparisons.objective: Assemble and mesh three gears on assigned shafts, versus set and lock an angular-gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-893 requires shaft insertion and tooth-phase discovery by contact; the candidate requires screw adjustment, jam-nut counterholding, and tool regrasping.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-893 requires three seated, meshed, still gears with arms clear; the candidate requires angle accuracy, locking, low drift, and repeated articulated motion.
comparisons.reason: Gear phasing and multi-part insertion are meaningfully different from adjustment retention under locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Reorient and stow a brad nailer without pointing it at a coworker or touching the trigger, versus adjust a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1467 tests safety-constrained transport and regrasping; the candidate tests coupled two-tool fastening and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1467 requires safe orientation throughout and final placement in a case; the candidate requires locked angle retention and successful motion cycles.
comparisons.reason: The nailer task's defining ability is continuous hazard-aware orientation control, absent from the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Open a folding-table leg, lock its brace ring, and withstand a side load, versus set and jam-lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1663 swings a linkage and slides a discrete ring over a knee; the candidate continuously adjusts a screw and counterholds it while tightening a concentric nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Both include hands-clear functional retention, but PR-1663 checks an open leg and brace under side load while the candidate checks retained opening angle across cycles.
comparisons.reason: The shared lock-and-test pattern is generic; sliding a brace sleeve on an articulated linkage does not test preserving a screw setting against tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Extract a jammed printer card intact and resume printing, versus adjust and lock a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1739 requires symmetric two-hand pulling to avoid skew and tearing; the candidate requires rotational tool coordination and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1739 scores intact extraction, placement, and an OK-button action; the candidate scores locked angular accuracy and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Balanced deformable-media extraction is unrelated to coupled screw-and-nut adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Set a telescoping gauge to a bore diameter and leave it retained on a stand, versus set a gripper opening stop and lock it.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1880 uses bore contact, gauge rocking, plunger locking, extraction, and placement; the candidate uses coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque against jam-nut reaction.
comparisons.success_condition: Both retain a calibrated setting after release, but PR-1880 requires a span within 0.10 mm and stand placement, while the candidate requires nut seating and repeated gripper actuation with limited drift.
comparisons.reason: Setting retention is shared, but contact metrology and withdrawing a telescoping gauge test a different physical ability from locking an adjustment screw under coupled torque.

comparisons.objective: Place a shackle around a towing lug and screw its pin fully home, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1886 requires multi-hole alignment, pin insertion, thread starting, and repeated regrasping; the candidate requires preserving a continuous screw setting while tightening its jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1886 requires the pin through all three holes, collar seated, and hand-tight; it does not require retention of a calibrated adjustment or functional cycling.
comparisons.reason: Threading is shared only as a generic primitive; the shackle task tests aligned assembly rather than counterheld adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Seat and tighten a positive battery-terminal clamp while preserving cable-lug alignment, versus set and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1947 holds/seats a clamp and operates one wrench; the candidate simultaneously seats a hex driver and open-end wrench on a coupled screw and jam nut to oppose tightening torque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1947 requires a seated, torqued clamp, aligned lug, safe wrench removal, and an unmoved battery; the candidate additionally requires a retained target angle over repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve tightening without disturbing alignment, battery-clamp installation does not test locking a continuous adjustment through coaxial countertorque and subsequent motion cycles.

comparisons.objective: Transfer and quarter-turn-lock an air-line gladhand to the correct trailer connector, versus set and jam-lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1960 requires hose handling, face alignment, seal compression, and bayonet rotation; the candidate requires two-tool screw/nut countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1960 requires the correct connector, small plate gap, lock-stop angle, pull retention, and release; the candidate requires angular-setting accuracy and cycle repeatability.
comparisons.reason: Connector mating and bayonet locking are different from preserving an adjustable stop while tightening a jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Reconfigure tongue-and-groove pliers from groove one to groove five and leave them locked, versus set and lock a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1985 opens the handles to disengage a tongue, slides a rivet to a discrete groove, and recloses; the candidate performs continuous screw adjustment with two-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1985 requires groove-five seating, resistance to a 5 N push, flat rest, and clearance; the candidate requires target angle, seated nuts, low stop drift, and three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both alter and retain a mechanism setting, but discrete groove release-slide-reengage does not test counterholding a screw against locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Align and press two boards together over three dowels, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2003 requires bimanual multi-axis insertion and even pressing across three pins; the candidate requires rotational tool seating and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2003 scores insertion depth, seam gaps, flush edges, flatness, release, and stillness; the candidate scores retained angular calibration and cycles.
comparisons.reason: Multi-dowel alignment and insertion are unrelated to adjustable-stop locking.

comparisons.objective: Hang and latch a telescoping server rail at the same rack U on front and rear posts, versus set and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2073 requires long-part support, peg alignment, telescoping extension, and two-end latching; the candidate requires localized two-tool countertorque and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2073 requires both ends latched at the marked U, levelness, release, and no fall; the candidate requires angle retention through repeated gripper cycles.
comparisons.reason: Rack-rail installation tests distributed alignment and latching, not preservation of a threaded adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Water soil while holding a springy leaf aside and avoiding wet leaves, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1272 requires simultaneous obstruction control and controlled pouring; the candidate requires coaxial fastener manipulation and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1272 scores delivered water, leaf contamination, restored leaf/jug positions, and arm clearance; the candidate scores mechanical setting and retained function.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual coordination is generic; liquid delivery around an obstruction is a different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Cut a cable tie from a bundle without damaging insulation, versus set and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1441 stabilizes a rolling bundle while precisely positioning and closing flush cutters; the candidate counterholds a screw while tightening a jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1441 requires complete tie removal, no cable nick, tool return, and bundle stability; the candidate requires retained angle and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Damage-avoiding cutting is meaningfully different from adjustment and locknut control.

comparisons.objective: Remove one interleaved tissue while leaving the next exposed and the box stable, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1673 requires delicate deformable-sheet extraction and force management; the candidate requires rigid two-tool rotational manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1673 scores one-sheet removal, tray placement, next-sheet presentation, box placement, and release; the candidate scores a locked angular setting.
comparisons.reason: Selective deformable separation is unrelated to screw-and-jam-nut adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Make a deli slicer safe, release its carriage, and place the carriage on a cleaning tray, versus set and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1850 requires ordered knob operations, carriage translation/lift, and avoidance of a blade zone; the candidate requires coupled tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1850 requires zero gauge opening before motion, release-knob travel, safe removal, tray placement, and clearance; the candidate requires retained opening angle across cycles.
comparisons.reason: Safety-conditioned disassembly and carriage handling test a different ability from locking an adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Hold a spring-backed valve cartridge fully home while inserting its retainer clip, versus set and jam-lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1905 uses one hand to oppose axial O-ring force while the other aligns and slides a U-clip; the candidate opposes rotational locknut reaction with a driver while tightening with a wrench.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1905 requires flush cartridge seating, fully seated clip, and retention under a 20 N pull; the candidate requires angular accuracy, nut retention, and repeatable actuation.
comparisons.reason: Both coordinate holding with locking, but axial part seating plus transverse clip insertion is a different tested mechanism and ability from countertorque-preserved screw adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Flex a 3D-printer build plate to release a printed part without kinking it, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1949 requires symmetric controlled elastic bending and part capture; the candidate requires rigid tool seating, turning, and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1949 requires part release into a bin, plate restoration, curvature safety, stillness, and clearance; the candidate requires retained angle and functional cycles.
comparisons.reason: Controlled elastic flexure and release are unrelated to threaded adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Fit a separate key and keyed pulley onto a freely rotating shaft, versus set and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2037 counterholds a shaft while placing a key, phase-aligning a pulley keyway, and sliding the pulley home; the candidate counterholds an adjustment screw while tightening its concentric jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2037 requires key seating, pulley insertion to the shoulder, release, and one-second stillness; the candidate requires nut locking and repeated retained-angle cycles.
comparisons.reason: Counterholding is shared, but keyed multi-part alignment and insertion are meaningfully different from preserving a continuous setting under tightening torque; no task.json spec was available, but the PR body provides the full staged rubric.

comparisons.objective: Spin lettuce dry by cranking a salad spinner while keeping the bowl stable, versus adjust and lock a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2051 requires one-hand fixture stabilization and repeated cyclic cranking with the other; the candidate requires precise two-tool countertorque and subsequent lever actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2051 scores crank turns or sustained basket speed, lid/bowl stability, and release; the candidate scores a calibrated locked stop and low drift over cycles.
comparisons.reason: Stabilized repetitive cranking does not test adjustment locking, despite both involving rotational actions.

comparisons.objective: Mount and align a dogbone specimen in two tensile-tester wedge grips at a specified gauge length, versus set and lock a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2186 requires two-ended specimen insertion, spring-lever operation, straightening, and crosshead jogging; the candidate requires coaxial screw/nut tool coordination and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2186 scores independent tab seating, lever closure, end clearances, 115 mm jaw spacing, alignment, clearance, and a three-second hold; the candidate requires retained stop angle and repeated gripper cycles.
comparisons.reason: Precision specimen fixturing in two clamps tests distributed insertion and alignment, not preservation of a threaded adjustment against locknut reaction.
